gaze_still.title: Look around the screen
gaze_still.instruction: With a comfortable head position, look at the center, corners and different areas of this screen. Stay within this screen.

gaze_turn.title: Look at the dot with slight head movements
gaze_turn.instruction: Keep looking at the central dot while gently moving your head left, right, up and down.

gaze_nod.title: Turn your head clearly away
gaze_nod.instruction: Turn your head comfortably to one side and hold it there so your eyes are no longer facing the camera. Do not strain your neck.

gaze_away.title: Look outside the screen
gaze_away.instruction: With your head comfortable and your eyes visible, look at a fixed object clearly outside this screen and hold your gaze there.

gaze_camera.title: Look directly at the lens
gaze_camera.instruction: Look directly at the camera lens and hold your gaze there. Keep the screen and camera in the same position.

gaze_still.title: Look at the dot with your head still
gaze_still.instruction: Keep a comfortable posture and look at the central dot.

gaze_turn.title: Look at the dot and turn your head slightly
gaze_turn.instruction: Keep looking at the central dot while gently turning your head left and right. Use small, comfortable movements.

gaze_nod.title: Look at the dot and nod gently
gaze_nod.instruction: Keep your eyes on the central dot while making small up-and-down head movements. Do not strain your neck.

gaze_away.title: Now look at the corner dot
gaze_away.instruction: Look at the upper-left dot while keeping your head comfortable. This example helps compare different gaze directions.

gaze_camera.title: Look directly at the lens
gaze_camera.instruction: Look at your laptop camera lens, centered above the screen. Keep a comfortable posture and the screen in the same position.

nod_still.title: Keep your head still
nod_still.instruction: Stay silent without nodding. This interval helps check whether the detector reports movements you did not make.

nod_three.title: Make three separate nods
nod_three.instruction: Make one gentle yes movement each time the number changes. Return to your normal posture after each nod and wait for the next number.

head_shake.title: Gently shake your head no
head_shake.instruction: Turn your head gently from side to side without nodding up and down. This checks whether the detector confuses the two movements.

smile_neutral.title: Relax your face
smile_neutral.instruction: Stay silent with relaxed lips, without smiling or pressing your lips together.

smile_speech.title: Speak without smiling
smile_speech.instruction: With a neutral expression, read: “Good morning, I would like to know how you have been feeling and what concerns you today.”

smile_silent.title: Smile without speaking
smile_silent.instruction: Show a natural, comfortable smile without speaking. You do not need to show your teeth.

smile_speech_positive.title: Speak while smiling
smile_speech_positive.instruction: With a natural smile, repeat: “Good morning, I would like to know how you have been feeling and what concerns you today.”

welcome.title: Before starting the interview
welcome.description: You will talk with a virtual patient to practice history taking and clinical communication. Take the role of a healthcare professional and conduct the interview as you would in a consultation.
welcome.scope: Scope: This activity is limited to history taking. No physical examination will be performed.
welcome.duration: Duration: Spend approximately 10 to 15 minutes on the interview. When you are done, select Finish and enter up to three diagnostic hypotheses based on the information obtained.
welcome.conversation: The patient will start with a greeting. Introduce yourself and explore the presenting complaint, symptoms, medical history and concerns. Send each contribution using the arrow button and wait for the patient's response.
welcome.devices: Keep your camera and microphone available, your face visible and the room well lit. Choose a quiet setting, keep a stable position and avoid resizing the window during the interview.
welcome.privacy: Do not share personal health information or real patient data. Use only the information from the simulated case.
welcome.evaluation: Assessment: Complete and submit your self-assessment. Once submitted, you can view the automatic assessment generated by the system.
welcome.begin: Accepting will start the timer and the patient's first turn.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.description: This virtual patient is an interactive educational tool designed to train medical students in clinical interviewing and communication skills.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: Practise taking a medical history in a simulated clinical interview and receive automated feedback on your performance.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.step1: Select a clinical case from the available scenarios
howItWorks.step2: Conduct a virtual interview with the AI-powered patient, asking questions and gathering information
howItWorks.step3: Submit your diagnostic hypotheses based on the information you gathered
howItWorks.step4: Review your assessment and feedback on communication and interview completeness

clinicalCases.title: Clinical cases
clinicalCases.description: The platform offers a variety of clinical cases covering different medical specialties and difficulty levels:
clinicalCases.feature1: Pre-built cases covering common medical conditions and scenarios
clinicalCases.feature2: Default case catalog available only for reading and interview practice.
clinicalCases.feature3: AI-powered patients with realistic personalities and responses

additionalInfo.description: This platform is developed by Universidad de los Andes, Colombia, as part of a research project in the Department of Systems and Computer Engineering. It utilizes AI technology to create realistic patient interactions and provide comprehensive educational feedback.
